scope: Euclidean straight-line Kakeya in dimensions n>=5, and the low-dimensional inputs relevant to the supplied OpenAI four-dimensional manuscript. This is a checked baseline, not an exhaustive bibliographic or priority search.

sources.title: Kakeya and Furstenberg problems for sticky sets of tubes
sources.version: arXiv:2609.22035v1; latest listed version checked as of 2026-10-16
claims_checked: Theorem 1.2 assumes a (3,delta^-eta)-AD-regular tube family in R^4, convex Wolff constant <=delta^-eta, and delta^eta-dense shading
Pages 3-4 explain that convex Wolff axioms alone are insufficient for general R^4 tube families, giving concentration near quadrics with union volume <=C delta^(1/2)
This obstacle does not itself disprove the direction-separated Kakeya conjecture
sources.proof_status: preprint statement and obstacle checked; full proof not audited
